source: Diocese of Northern Michigan Cycle of Prayer 2026
sourceFile: Diocesan resource page, fetched directly from https://upepiscopal.org/diocesan-cycle-of-prayer/ (12 month sections, each headed by a bare month name and a bulleted list giving only the day-of-month plus subject -- no year or weekday name printed anywhere on the page).
notes: IMPORTANT: this is the Episcopal Diocese of NORTHERN Michigan (Marquette, covering the Upper Peninsula), a separate diocese from the Diocese of Michigan already held in this corpus as episcopal-michigan-2026.json. dioceseShort is 'northern-michigan', deliberately distinct from that file's 'michigan'. The cycle's own February 15 entry even names 'Diocese of Michigan' as a separate prayer subject -- see below -- confirming the two dioceses are distinct in the source's own eyes, not a naming collision introduced here.

The source page prints no calendar year or weekday name on any entry -- only a month heading (e.g. 'January') followed by a bulleted list of bare day-of-month numbers (e.g. '4', '11', '18', '25'). cycleType 'dated' was used, not 'monthly-recurring' or 'ordinal-sunday-monthly', because every one of the 52 (month, day-of-month) pairs the source prints resolves to an actual Sunday of calendar year 2026 when checked (verified programmatically against a real calendar before transcribing) -- i.e. this is a real dated 52-Sunday cycle for 2026, the source is simply printing each date as 'day-of-month under its month heading' rather than spelling out 'January 4, 2026'. The `date` field in each entry below is this app's own resolution of that pairing to ISO form, not an invention of content the source didn't provide.

Congregation names are transcribed exactly as this cycle-of-prayer page itself prints them, which for several entries is a shorter/less formal form than the diocese's own separate 'Churches' page (upepiscopal.org/churches/): e.g. this cycle says 'Trinity Church, Iron Mountain' where the Churches page gives 'Holy Trinity Episcopal Church' for Iron Mountain; this cycle says 'St. Stephen's Church, DeTour' where the Churches page gives 'De Tour Village, St. Stephen's Episcopal Church'. Per this corpus's standing rule, the cycle-of-prayer document's own wording is transcribed as printed, not normalized/expanded to match the separate Churches page.

May 3, 'Breaking Bread at Jack's, Rapid River', is recorded as a `category` subject (not `parish`) with the full string as its `name`, not split into name+place: per the diocese's own 'Churches' page, this is listed under 'Our Communities' as 'a dinner fellowship called Breaking Bread' at Rapid River, distinct from the page's 19 listed congregations under 'Our Congregations' -- it is a named ministry, not a specific congregation, even though (like a parish) it names a town.

April 19, 'UP Wild', is recorded as a `category` subject for the same reason: the diocese's 'Churches' page lists 'U.P. Wild' groups (outdoor prayer communities in several counties) under 'Our Communities', not 'Our Congregations'.

Every other subject not naming one of the diocese's 19 listed congregations (diocesan-wide ministries/offices, Indigenous tribal communities in the diocese's territory, ecumenical/civic observances, other dioceses named for prayer, etc.) is recorded as `category` with the source's own text as `name` verbatim, including its own internal punctuation (e.g. 'Neighboring Diocese: Algoma (Ontario)', 'International Day for Peace, Sept. 21 (U.N.)').

Minor HTML markup artifacts in the source (double spaces before some subjects, e.g. '28  Our Nation'; a subject's text occasionally wrapped in a stray inline <span> tag with its own trailing space, e.g. after 'UP Wild ' and 'St. Mark's Church, Crystal Falls ') are collapsed/trimmed as ordinary whitespace formatting, not treated as a content typo to preserve -- the wording itself is transcribed unchanged.

November 15 ('Christ Church, Calumet') duplicates June 21's entry -- the same congregation is simply named twice in the source's own 52-week rotation; transcribed as printed both times, not deduplicated.
